title: South West Water given lowest environmental rating
summary:
South West Water has been given the lowest possible environmental rating by the Environment Agency over high levels of pollution.
The regulator downgraded the firm from two stars out of a possible four to one, meaning it is now considered a "poor performing company" for its environmental impact.
South West Water, which has 1.8 million customers across Devon, Cornwall, the Isles of Scilly and parts of Dorset and Somerset, said it knew there was "much more to do" and was taking action to improve areas that "matter most" to customers and the environment.
The annual Environmental Performance Assessment grades England's nine water and sewerage companies largely on how often they pollute rivers, streams and the sea.
For 2025, South West Water was among four companies rated as poor performing, or one star, while four others were rated as requiring improvement, two stars.

title: Montana acquires sustainable furniture maker Takt
summary:
Montana has announced its buyout of fellow Danish design brand Takt, known for its solid wood furniture and pioneering approach to sustainable design.
Founded in 2019 by trained physicist and former Lego and Bang & Olufsen executive Henrik Taudorf Lorensen, Takt makes modern Scandinavian furniture from FSC-certified wood that is low-carbon, flat-pack and designed for disassembly.
“Takt brings experience with materials and the environment, and we are looking forward to bringing our respective experience together and taking this work even further,” he said.
By gaining access to the established, international infrastructure of Montana, which has been operating since 1982, Lorensen hopes that Takt’s furniture will be able to reach a larger audience.
““Now it is time for TAKT’s next chapter, and we are delighted that it will be written together with Montana.”

title: UK weather: 10 days without rain after 'wettest week in two years'
summary:
The UK could see as many as 10 consecutive days without rain after an unsettled end to October that featured back-to-back storms.
It comes after the Environment Agency said England experienced its wettest week in two years thanks to Storms Austen and Boelo.
Following this recent unsettled weather, the return of high pressure will bring a prolonged spell of largely dry and calm conditions, with very little rain in sight.
Mist and fog will remain a persistent feature, with some slow-clearing dense patches expected during the mornings.

title: RAF base chemical contamination worst in UK, report finds
summary:
Chemical contamination at a former RAF base earmarked for 9,000 homes is the worst found in the UK, a report has said.
Testing at RAF Upper Heyford carried out on behalf of a developer found "unacceptable" levels of polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), referred to as forever chemicals.
At RAF Upper Heyford, firefighters would practice putting out an aeroplane set on fire above a "pond" of fuel.
This training area was found to be "the most significant ongoing source of PFAS contamination identified" - a few hundred metres north of existing developments.
Another report into ground and surface water found contamination was "widespread" at the site, with all samples exceeding environmental standards.
